text: {"features":[{"name":"Mission alignment","description":"How clearly the letter shows understanding of this specific role's mandate to automate and scale security work through backend systems, AI agents, and vulnerability response at Google scale.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Expresses only generic interest in security or infrastructure and makes little connection to the actual responsibilities of this role."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Names the role and one relevant theme, but the motivation remains broad and could fit many backend or security jobs."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Connects the application to several relevant themes such as secure development, security tooling, or foundational impact, without showing especially sharp insight into the team's mandate."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows clear understanding of the role's focus on automating security processes or vulnerability handling at scale and explains why that work specifically appeals."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Articulates a precise and compelling fit with the role by linking security automation, AI agents, vulnerability response, or Google-wide leverage into a coherent reason for applying."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement orientation","description":"How strongly the letter frames security work as helping developer teams adopt secure defaults through usable tooling rather than adding friction.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Treats security mainly as protection or rigor in the abstract, with no clear attention to helping other engineers work more securely."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Briefly mentions developers or best practices, but does not show a concrete enablement mindset."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Indicates that the candidate values making security easier for engineers, though the idea is not central or well developed."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Clearly emphasizes secure defaults, reduced friction, or helping teams do the right thing through tooling and process design."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes developer enablement a defining theme of the letter, showing a nuanced view that good security tooling changes defaults, removes toil, and supports busy engineering teams."}]},{"name":"Software engineering depth","description":"How much substantive professional experience the letter presents in testing, maintaining, launching, and owning production software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Presents only near-minimum experience with limited scope of shipped systems or ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows solid early-career production experience, but with modest scope, few services, or little sense of sustained ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows a clear mid-level background with multiple years and multiple production services across testing, maintenance, and launches."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong depth through several years of production work plus evidence of repeated launches or broad ownership of important services."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows especially deep and credible production experience, combining substantial years, repeated service ownership, and clear exposure to the full lifecycle of shipping and operating software."}]},{"name":"Go backend fit","description":"How convincingly the letter presents Go as a central language for production backend or infrastructure work relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mentions Go only in passing or as one language among many, with no sense of depth or role relevance."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Indicates some Go use at work, but only in generic terms that do not establish it as a core strength."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular Go use in production services, but with limited detail beyond that."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents Go as a primary or chief language for multiple production backend or infrastructure systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents Go as a major production strength and ties it directly to role-relevant backend systems such as services, control layers, or guardrail infrastructure."}]},{"name":"Python engineering fit","description":"How convincingly the letter presents Python as a production language for tooling, automation, services, or agents relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention Python or mentions it so indirectly that no meaningful Python fit is established."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python only briefly or as lightweight scripting, with little evidence of production use."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, or prototypes, but not much depth beyond that."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows substantial Python use in production systems or internal services relevant to automation or analysis work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows deep, production-grade Python work that is central to automation, tooling, or agent-based systems."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic strength","description":"How strongly the letter evidences skill with data structures and algorithms through concrete technical examples.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no meaningful evidence of algorithmic work or mentions it only as a buzzword."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims algorithmic competence in broad terms without a concrete example or clear effect."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides one concrete example of using data structures or algorithms to improve a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Provides a specific and technically credible example showing thoughtful algorithmic reasoning on a meaningful performance or correctness problem."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes algorithmic strength unmistakable through a clear, high-leverage example that shows both technical judgment and material system improvement."}]},{"name":"Security assessment maturity","description":"How convincingly the letter shows experience performing structured security assessments such as threat modeling, code review, or validating fixes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of doing security assessments or only implies a general security interest."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Suggests limited or informal security review experience without describing scope or method."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States experience performing security assessments and names relevant activities such as threat modeling or code review."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes structured security assessment work with credible scope, method, or lessons drawn from it."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows mature assessment capability by describing hands-on, builder-aware security review work and how that perspective informs system design or remediation."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability triage automation","description":"How directly the letter shows experience building automation for intake, classification, deduplication, routing, or handling of vulnerability reports.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no evidence of automating vulnerability handling and speaks only generally about security work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security automation in broad terms without a specific vulnerability-triage example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States a direct example of automating vulnerability report intake or routing, but with limited detail on the workflow."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes a clear vulnerability-triage system with multiple steps such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, or routing."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents vulnerability-triage automation as a meaningful owned accomplishment that materially reduced manual work or turned a painful queue into a scalable pipeline."}]},{"name":"Agentic tooling design","description":"How well the letter demonstrates design experience with agent-based systems, especially Python agents governed by backend constraints or auditability.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention agentic systems or only references AI in generic terms."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents in passing without explaining architecture, boundaries, or responsibilities."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States experience designing agentic tooling and identifies roles for agents and services at a high level."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes a credible agentic architecture with Python agents plus Go services providing supervision, permissions, logging, or guardrails."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows strong agentic-systems judgment by explaining bounded autonomy, auditability, and clear separation between agent behavior and backend control infrastructure."}]},{"name":"Applied AI engineering","description":"How convincingly the letter shows practical experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality in production with attention to reliability.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention AI experience or mentions AI only as an area of interest."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI or LLMs briefly without showing production use or engineering responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States direct experience building AI-backed features in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows production AI experience plus some attention to trustworthiness, evaluation, or failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents AI work as a mature engineering practice, emphasizing shipping model-backed systems responsibly under real reliability constraints."}]},{"name":"Offensive security engagement","description":"How much the letter demonstrates attacker-oriented security practice through certifications, competition, exploitation, or similar hands-on work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no attacker-oriented security signal beyond general security interest."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a modest signal such as occasional CTF participation or a baseline certification."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear extra depth through regular CTF participation, a stronger certification, or explicit attacker-style thinking."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows substantial offensive-security engagement through OSCP-level work, strong CTF results, or sustained exploitation practice."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows unusually strong attacker-oriented credibility through multiple substantial signals or especially demanding hands-on offensive experience."}]},{"name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"How much the letter shows responsibility for contributing to or maintaining open-source software in a way that signals collaboration and engineering discipline.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no open-source evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional bug fixes or patches with little sense of ongoing responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular upstream contribution or maintenance of a small open-source effort."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows meaningful maintainership or an actively used project with contribution review or release responsibility."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows strong open-source stewardship through sustained maintenance of a real user-facing project or framework and clear ownership of interface, review, and releases."}]},{"name":"Personal engineering initiative","description":"How strongly the letter uses self-directed technical projects outside work to show curiosity, ownership, and system-building ability.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no personal project evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small side project, but it appears lightweight or only loosely relevant to the role."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a personal project that shows initiative and some technical substance."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes an ambitious or technically demanding side project that reinforces relevant systems or reliability skills."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Describes a sustained, highly challenging self-directed system build that strongly strengthens the technical case for the role."}]},{"name":"Concrete evidence","description":"How much the letter supports its claims with specific examples, scope, mechanisms, or observable outcomes rather than generic assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mostly on broad claims and aspirations with little concrete evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Includes a few specifics such as years or tools, but most strengths remain asserted rather than demonstrated."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives several concrete examples of work, though outcomes or scope are not consistently clear."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Regularly grounds claims in specific systems, tasks, or technical wins that make the case easy to evaluate."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Builds nearly every major claim on concrete, credible evidence, often showing both what was done and why it mattered."}]},{"name":"Structural coherence","description":"How clearly the letter is organized into a readable, logically progressing argument for fit.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Feels choppy, list-like, or hard to follow, with little clear progression from motivation to evidence to close."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has a basic structure but uneven transitions or abrupt topic shifts that weaken the case."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Is generally coherent and easy to follow, though the narrative is more functional than polished."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Flows well from motivation through evidence to conclusion, with purposeful sequencing and smooth transitions."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Reads as a tightly constructed argument whose structure steadily strengthens the candidate's fit from opening to close."}]},{"name":"Proofreading accuracy","description":"How free the letter is from spelling, typographical, and obvious mechanical errors that distract from credibility.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Contains frequent visible errors that repeatedly distract or force rereading."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Contains numerous noticeable errors, but the meaning usually remains recoverable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Contains a moderate number of errors that are noticeable but not dominant."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Contains only a few minor errors that rarely interrupt reading."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Is essentially clean and carefully proofread, with little or no distracting error."}]},{"name":"Persuasive voice","description":"How effectively the letter projects a confident, professional, and memorable voice rather than sounding generic or formulaic.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Feels bland, mechanical, or disconnected, with little sense of conviction or individual perspective."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has some professional tone but remains generic, stiff, or only weakly engaging."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Presents a credible professional voice with occasional memorable phrasing or authentic motivation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Feels confident and engaging, with a clear point of view that supports the application without sounding forced."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Delivers a distinctive and persuasive voice that makes the application feel both highly professional and genuinely compelling."}]}]}
